2.text: had to be kept carefully tied all the time. The Siberian harness-dogs are

3.text: more given to howling than barking. Their howl is long and whining, and

4.text: ends with an occasional yelp. On winter nights the whole canine population

5.text: of the village, often several hundred head strong, will raise a chorus that will

6.text: last for half an hour, subsiding several times, and then breaking out again.

8.text: especially in the spring. I observed that it occurred most frequently after a

9.text: long course on the open tundra; and, according to native ideas, it results

10.text: from the action upon the brain of the excessive brightness of the snow, analogous

11.text: to the spring snow-blindness of men. Dog-rabies, however, is not so bad in

12.text: northern as in southern latitudes; and, though I have known of many men

13.text: being bitten by a rabid dog, I have never heard of any bad results from the

14.text: bite, but I have heard of some such cases with rabid wolves. However, any

15.text: dog bitten by a rabid one will itself go mad, and sometimes, when the rabid

16.text: dog is not killed in time, several teams will be greatly injured. On long

17.text: journeys the drivers simply muzzle the rabid dogs at first, so that they cannot

18.text: bite their companions; and they continue to drive them thus for two or three

19.text: successive days, as I witnessed when travelling among the Chukchee between

30.text: DOG-DRIVING. — The dog-sledge now in use in northeastern Siberia (Fig. 21)
30.note: Run-in heading set in small capitals (ᴅᴏɢ-ᴅʀɪᴠɪɴɢ. confirmed at 2× zoom), second-level per keying_spec.md §2.13, keyed in plain ASCII capitals.

31.text: is long and narrow, and has three or four pairs of stanchions. The lower end

32.text: of the stanchion is cut off square, except a rough peg which is left standing

33.text: in the middle. The peg is inserted in a circular hole in the runner (Fig. 21, b).

34.text: Each pair of stanchions is joined at half their height by a round stick, which

35.text: is mortised into a circular hole in the stanchion. A thin, broad plank — or

36.text: rather two planks laced together — rests on these sticks. Two rails are fastened

37.text: on the upper ends of the stanchions, and are lashed to the boards with thong,

38.text: which forms a kind of retaining-net all around the sledge. The runners are

39.text: flat, and their front ends are strongly curved and tied to a strong wooden bow,

40.text: which is fastened to the foremost stanchions with strong lashings (Fig. 21, c).
